title: A Superconducting Phase Transition Single-Electron Transistor
authors: Gorka Aizpurua-Iraola, Thomas H. Swift, Felix-Ekkehard von Horstig, Domenic Prete, James Kirkman, Grayson M. Noah, Fabio Olivieri, Alberto Gomez-Saiz, M. Fernando Gonzalez-Zalba
abstract: Quantum computers require fast and accurate methods for qubit state detection. Phase-transition sensors exploit the abrupt change between two physical states of a material to achieve enhanced sensitivity and have enabled advanced detectors for quantum technologies, such as superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors. However, this sensing principle has not yet been applied to semiconductor spin qubits. Here, we demonstrate a superconducting phase-transition radio-frequency single-electron transistor (PTSET), a charge sensor for semiconductor spin qubits whose response is enhanced by a superconducting-to-normal phase transition. The transition is engineered by linking the sensor current to a low-critical-current, high-kinetic-inductance inductor integrated into the radio-frequency matching network. We demonstrate improvements in sensitivity of one and two orders of magnitude over conventional rfSETs in the large- and small-signal regimes, respectively. Our results establish phase-transition sensing as a route towards ultrasensitive, integrated charge sensors for semiconductor quantum computing and point to broader applications, including cryogenic photon detection for radio astronomy.
summary: This paper introduces the Phase-Transition Single-Electron Transistor (PTSET) as a novel, highly sensitive charge sensor for semiconductor spin qubits. By exploiting the abrupt impedance change during a superconducting-to-normal phase transition, the device achieves significant sensitivity enhancements over existing readout technologies. This establishes a promising, integrated route for next-generation quantum computing hardware.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for ultrasensitive, integrated charge sensors to improve qubit state detection in semiconductor spin qubits.
main_result: The Superconducting Phase Transition Single-Electron Transistor (PTSET) demonstrates sensitivity improvements of one to two orders of magnitude over conventional rfSETs.
method: The authors measured the change in reflected power ($\Delta\Gamma$) as the SET current forces a superconducting-to-normal phase transition in an integrated circuit.
model_or_system: The system is a PTSET, integrating a Single-Electron Transistor (SET) with a superconducting inductor whose state changes abruptly when the bias current exceeds the critical current ($I_c$).
key_observables: Change in reflected power ($\Delta\Gamma$), minimum integration time ($t_{\min}$), and Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR).
important_parameters: Critical current ($I_c$), coupling capacitance ($C_C$), and the ratio of signal to noise power.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes certain conditions for noise power and approximates the SET resistance in the 'on' state for theoretical modeling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the PTSET principle, showing the superconducting vs. normal state impedance change; they also plot SNR vs. coupling capacitance and $t_{\min}$ vs. bias voltage, demonstrating the enhancement.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical principle of PTSET, demonstrates the enhanced sensing capability through measurements of $\Delta\Gamma$ and $t_{\min}$, and theoretically quantifies the resulting SNR improvement over standard rfSETs.
why_interesting: The work directly addresses a critical component of quantum computing infrastructure—high-fidelity, low-power readout electronics—by coupling quantum measurement principles to superconducting phenomena.
